items.text: REFERRED TO CIVIL SERVICE AND PENSIONS

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5557

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
removing limitations pertaining to certain retirees earnings


 PURPOSE :
This legislation removes the reference to subdivision c of section 605
of the retirement and social security law from section 607-b of the
retirement and social security law.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This bill would remove the reference to subdivision c of section 605
of the retirement and social security law from section 607-b of the
retirement and social security law.

 EXISTING LAW :
In May 2008, the New York City Employees' Retirement System (NYCERS)
promulgated a reinterpretation of RSSL §607-b pertaining to
post-retirement earnings limitations for EMT's employed by the City of
New York or by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation
found eligible for performance of duty disability pensions. This
resulted in the Unions of the affected members suing the City and the
retirement system. The parties reached an agreement to seek
sponsorship for legislation in the state legislature to remedy the
problem.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Section 607-b of the retirement and social security law was added in
1998 to provide a performance of duty disability benefit for employees
of the city of New York or the New York City health and hospitals
corporation who were injured in the performance of their duties as
emergency medical technicians or advanced emergency medical
technicians. These individuals may be able to be gainfully employed
despite the fact they are unable to perform emergency medical
technician work as a result of their injury. This bill would clarify
conflicting interpretations of the law to allow emergency medical
technicians and advanced emergency medical technicians to work in
non-emergency medical technician employment, and remove the bar to any
gainful employment currently set forth in section 605-c. The bill
codifies that which had been the practice for ten years since the
enactment of section 607-b.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
According to the actuary of the City of New York the change in
employer costs and employer contributions to NYCERS to be de minimis.
As of June 30th, 2008 there were approximately 230 EMT with retired on
accidental disability who could potentially be impacted by this
proposed legislation.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately and shall be deemed to have been in full force and effect
on and after January 1, 2009.

summary: Removes limitations pertaining to emergency medical technicians or advanced emergency medical technicians NYC retirees earnings.
